units.translation: In M is written Τυνδάρέω [Tyndareos], the letter w made from ao by a light stroke of the pen and the accent, which is over the e, crossed through with a line: by which a threefold spelling is indicated, Τυνδαρέα [Tyndarea], Τυνδάρεω [Tyndareo], Τυνδαρέου [Tyndareou], of which the last Τυνδαρέου [Tyndareou], which is also found here and there in the manuscripts of Euripides and others, has the least authority. Correct is Τυνδάρεω [Tyndareo]: unless Aeschylus wrote, which I do not believe, Τυνδαρέα [Tyndarea], as Euripides Iph. T. 5. said τῆς Τυνδαρείας θυγατρός [of the daughter of Tyndareus], and Aristoph. Thesm. 919. τῆς Τυνδαρείας παιδός [of the child of Tyndareus]. The forms of adjectives in coc for eloc, some of which Arcadius noted p. 39, 6, the scribes often obliterated, generally substituting the ending loc: so that it is uncertain whether Aeschylus Ag. 1499. wrote Ἀγαμεμνονίαν ἄλοχον [the wife of Agamemnon] and Ch. 861. Ἀγαμεμνονίων οἴκων [the house of Agamemnon] or Ἀγαμεμνονέαν [Agamemnonian] and Ἀγαμεμνονέων [Agamemnonian], which form alone Homer used.
And the image of a drum, as of underground thunder, comes heavily terrifying.
The form and great figure of Hippomedon.
Nor will I liken them to Gorgon figures.

Taking him in robes with a black-horned device she strikes.
He struck him with a charioteer's goad, grasping it in the middle, under the midriff.
For struck in the very midriff.
Struck through the left side. Struck indeed.
He licked his fill of royal blood.
Having died in a manner not royal.
Of him who holds the kingship
For this disease is somehow inherent in tyranny.
The one who helped establish the tyranny.
Who will cast him out from tyranny and his throne, unseen.
By whom it is fated that he fall from tyranny.
Practicing the signs of tyranny against the city.
For the fate of tyranny is riper.
Where then are the tyrannies of the dead?
Behold the double tyranny of the land.
For he is young and a tyrant among the gods.
The servant of the young tyrant.
Did I not perceive from these things that two tyrants have fallen?
As if you will be a tyrant of the Argives to me.
And the attendant of the greatest of the chthonic tyrants there.
By whom will the tyrant's scepter be plundered?
Similar is what Hesychius noted: σύρβα [tumultuously]: μετὰ θορύβου [with uproar].
Shaking and turning things turbulently up and down.
(from an elegy) The Tyrrhenian (should be written Τυρσηνόν [Tyrrhenian]. Bergkius: Τυρρηνῶν [of the Tyrrhenians]) race, a drug-making people.
